newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close mostly down after new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close mostly down after new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures failed to hold gains after posting new contract highs in August through December contracts early and values ended mostly lower to sharply lower on profit taking and spreading, traders said.

Live cattle closed unchanged to 0.775 cent per lb lower with only August unchanged at 67.650 cents. August set a new high of 68.325 cents early. Feeder cattle ended off 0.975 to 0.650 with August off 0.900 cent at 81.125 cents per lb.
August live cattle were underpinned by a strong tone to cash cattle markets, but most months fell as expectations were for cash prices to turn down later, traders said.

Spreaders bought August live cattle and sold October based on the cash strength, especially with heavy-weight choice beef values up to the highest level since May 6 and fed cattle selling $2 higher at $66 per cwt. August traded up to a new high with October and December following until profit taking developed and selling interest increased in back months.

"Deferred contracts recognize the fact that this (cash strength) is not going to last forever," said Chuck Levitt, livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp. "Once (retailers) get their Labor Day holiday needs satisfied, which takes about half way through August, that could be it for awhile."

R.J. O'Brien, Cargill Investor Services and Rosenthal Collins bought August early but R.J. O'Brien sold August at the close. Refco sold October late while Term and RBH sold October early, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commission houses sold August 68 calls. Commercials were rolling hedges, buying August 67 calls and selling October 71 calls. Commercials bought October 68 puts and December 70 puts late, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures were weighed down by rising corn futures with late sell stops pushing prices down to day's lows by the close, traders said.
The recent strength in corn offset a rise in the CME feeder cattle index, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.44 at $82.56 per cwt, highest level since March 4, 1994.

Dean Witter and LIT division of First Options spread long September short August. Cargill earlier spread long April live cattle/short November feeders and long August feeders/short December live cattle, pit sources added.

Boneless beef futures continued to show strength and set new highs in all months and beef trimmings also turned up after they recently fell to near par with cash. Spreaders bought trimmings while selling live cattle futures, traders said.
Lind-Waldock bought August trimmings and sold October live cattle. Rosenthal Collins bought boack months of both boneless beef and trimmings, they said.

Boneless beef futures closed 1.00 to 3.00 cent per lb higher with August up 1.50 at 103.00, a new contract high. Trimmings ended 0.20 to 3.00 highwer with August up 0.50 at 46.50 cents. December and April trimmings also set new highs.
